transcript.text: w/m finally died after 12 yrs, whats the best one to buy under £400? family of 5

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. For a family of five and a £400 ceiling, I would aim for a 9 kg, 1400 rpm freestanding washing machine rather than chasing extra features. That is usually the best capacity/value point: enough for family loads and bedding without the higher price of a 10–11 kg model. Prioritise, in this order:
1. A 9 kg drum and 1400 rpm spin.
2. A known UK brand with straightforward local warranty support and readily available spares; check the included guarantee and the cost of an extension before buying.
3. Dimensions and door clearance: measure the space, including hoses behind it and the door opening, before ordering.
4. A quick 30–60 minute wash, delay timer and an easy-clean pump filter. Wi-Fi and steam functions are less important at this budget.
5. Sensible noise ratings if it is near a living area; avoid choosing purely on the advertised programme count. I would not pay extra just for a 10 kg drum or app control under £400. Prices and model ranges change frequently, so compare the current 9 kg/1400 rpm options from established makers at the retailer on warranty, dimensions and delivery/installation rather than assuming one named model is always best. Before replacing the old one, it may be worth a quick check: try a different appliance in the washing-machine socket, or try the machine in a known-good socket only if it can be done safely without extension leads. If the socket/circuit is the issue, the machine may not be the culprit. If it powers up, a door-lock, drain or control fault can still be repairable even at 12 years old; whether it is worth repairing depends on what it actually does.
it does power on, socket's fine. it stopped mid-cycle 2 days ago with water still in the drum, won't drain or spin, just hums. would fix if its cheap, what should i check?

This is quite possibly a cheap fix. Water left in the drum plus a humming sound when it should drain points first to a blocked pump filter/foreign object, then a kinked drain hose; only after those are ruled out does a failed drain pump become the likely repair. It will not spin while it still detects water. 1. Switch off and unplug it. Put towels down and use a shallow tray. With water still in the drum, opening the filter can release a lot of water, so use any little emergency drain hose if fitted, or follow the draining method in the manual before unscrewing the filter. 2. Open the small flap/kick-panel at the bottom front and remove the pump filter slowly. Clear coins, hair grips, lint, buttons etc. Shine a torch into the opening: the small impeller behind it should move with gentle finger pressure and not be solidly jammed or visibly broken. A trapped item is the best-case, free repair. 3. Check the drain hose at the rear is not crushed or sharply kinked, and that the standpipe/sink-waste connection is not blocked. A humming pump with no flow can be caused by either restriction. If the filter and hose are clear but the pump still only hums and shifts no water, the drain pump is likely jammed internally or failing. That is normally a modest parts repair, but replacement involves access from underneath or behind panels, so an engineer is sensible unless you are confident with appliance dismantling. Do not order a pump until the filter and hose checks are done.
didn't know there was a filter tbh. water's still in the drum so will unplug first. haven't checked the hose either, will try both

That is the right order. The retained water is why it will not spin; the likely causes remain a blocked filter/trapped object first, then a kinked or blocked drain hose, with a failed pump only if those are clear. 1. Unplug it, turn off the water supply if convenient, and put plenty of towels plus a shallow tray in front of the lower flap. Water may come out quickly. If there is a small emergency drain tube, use that first; otherwise loosen the filter cap only a little at a time and empty the tray repeatedly. 2. Remove and clean the filter. Look for coins, hair grips, buttons, lint or fabric. With the filter out, use a torch and gently feel the little impeller just behind it: it should not be solidly jammed or have broken vanes. A trapped item or blocked filter is usually the cheap/free fix. 3. Check the grey drain hose at the back is not crushed or sharply bent, then check the point where it enters the standpipe or sink waste is not blocked. A clear filter but a restricted hose/waste gives the same no-drain symptom. Do not run a drain/spin test until the filter is back in straight and fully tightened, otherwise it can leak. Tell me whether you find debris, a jammed impeller, or a clear filter and hose; that will separate a simple blockage from a pump that may need repair.
ok will go and look now. any lights flashing is that useful? some were flashing on it, dunno which. model is WMBF944P if that matters

Yes — flashing lights can be useful, especially if they form a repeating pattern, as they can indicate a drainage fault. For now, the water remaining in the drum and the humming still make a restriction at the filter/pump path the leading possibility; the drain hose/waste blockage and the pump itself are next. 1. Which labelled lights are flashing, and whether they flash together or in a sequence.
2. Anything found in the filter, and whether the small impeller behind it is free to move or solidly jammed. That should tell us whether this is likely to be a free blockage clear-out or whether the pump needs further attention. Keep it unplugged while opening the filter and checking the impeller.
dunno which lights, just some flashing, didn't note the pattern. will check the filter and report back

The flashing lights may help if they recur, but without the pattern they do not narrow it down reliably. If they flash again, take a photo or short video before switching it off. For now, the retained water and humming still point most strongly to a blockage at the filter/pump, then a restricted drain hose or waste connection; a drain-pump failure is the next possibility if both are clear. When you have checked, let me know whether you find debris, whether the impeller is jammed or damaged, and whether the rear drain hose is kinked. That will tell us whether it is likely to be a free clear-out or whether the pump needs an engineer.
ok, off to check the filter now, will report back

The most likely causes are still a blocked filter/trapped item first, then a restriction in the drain hose or household waste; if both are clear, the drain pump becomes the more likely cheap-to-moderate repair. When you are back, report just these two things:
1. Whether anything came out of the filter, and whether the small impeller behind it turns without being solidly jammed or damaged.
2. Whether the rear drain hose is kinked/crushed, or its connection to the waste looks blocked. That result will tell us whether to try a drain-and-spin test after refitting the filter, or whether it is time to consider a pump repair rather than replacing the machine.
ok, still going to check it now, will report back once I've looked at the filter and hose

No problem — take your time. The most likely outcome is still a blockage in the filter/pump area; after that, an obstructed or kinked drain hose, then the drain pump itself. When you are back, just let me know: 1) what came out of the filter and whether the impeller moved, and 2) whether the rear drain hose looked kinked or blocked. That will tell us whether it is likely to be a free fix or a modest pump repair.
